definitions.title: Pause & Reflect
definitions.purpose: Use the Body / Mind / Life model to notice where tinnitus is affecting you right now.
definitions.instructions: Use a few words or longer notes. This reflection is for noticing patterns, not diagnosing yourself.

fields.label: Before you write
fields.helperText: Use the Body / Mind / Life model to notice where tinnitus is affecting you right now. A short note is enough.

fields.label: Body
fields.prompt: In my body, I notice…
fields.helperText: This might include hearing, sound sensitivity, tension, fatigue, stress physiology, or other physical factors.

fields.label: Mind
fields.prompt: In my mind, I notice…
fields.helperText: This might include attention, thoughts, emotions, worry, or meaning.

fields.label: Life
fields.prompt: In my daily life, I notice…
fields.helperText: This might include sleep, routines, work, relationships, places, or activities.

fields.label: Support
fields.prompt: One area I may want to support first is…
fields.helperText: Choose one area that feels useful to start with. You can change this later.

definitions.title: Sound Therapy Sweet Spot Reflection
definitions.purpose: Reflect on the middle range where sound therapy is audible and useful without fully covering tinnitus.
definitions.instructions: Use words rather than exact volume numbers. Avoid unsafe loudness; sound therapy should stay comfortable.

fields.label: Comfort boundary
fields.helperText: The sweet spot is not a test of toughness. If sound feels painful, unsafe, or sharply uncomfortable, lower it or stop and consider hearing-care guidance.

fields.label: Sound used
fields.prompt: Example: rain, fan, music, broadband sound
fields.helperText: Name the sound or sound category you tried.

fields.label: Setting or context
fields.prompt: Where or when did you try it?
fields.helperText: A short setting note is enough.

fields.label: Too quiet note
fields.prompt: What did too quiet feel like, if you noticed?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Sweet spot note
fields.prompt: What felt audible, comfortable, and useful?
fields.helperText: Describe the middle range in practical words.

fields.label: Too loud or overmasking note
fields.prompt: What told you the sound was too much?
fields.helperText: Optional. This is about comfort, not pushing through.

fields.label: Plan adjustment
fields.prompt: What might you adjust next time?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: Sound Sensitivity Exercise
definitions.purpose: Create a controlled, comfortable sound-sensitivity practice using enjoyable music on speakers.
definitions.instructions: This is not about pushing through pain. Keep sound comfortable, controlled, and below the sensitivity point.

fields.label: Comfort-first practice
fields.helperText: Start low, increase gradually only while comfortable, then back down below the point of sensitivity. Stop if sound becomes painful or unsafe.

fields.label: Music choice
fields.prompt: What enjoyable music did you choose?
fields.helperText: Choose something pleasant or neutral.

fields.label: Starting volume note
fields.prompt: How did you begin?
fields.helperText: Optional. Starting all the way down is fine.

fields.label: Comfortable below sensitivity level
fields.prompt: How did you know the level stayed comfortable?
fields.helperText: Use practical body or attention cues, not a number.

fields.label: Listening duration note
fields.prompt: How long did you listen?
fields.helperText: Optional. A short practice can count.

fields.label: What I noticed
fields.prompt: What did you notice during or after listening?
fields.helperText: Keep this nonjudgmental.

fields.label: Nonjudgmental takeaway
fields.prompt: What is one gentle takeaway?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: Personalized Sound Therapy Plan
definitions.purpose: Choose sounds, devices, times, and contexts for a practical sound therapy plan.
definitions.instructions: Keep the plan small and realistic. This is educational planning, not a treatment prescription.

fields.label: Preferred sound
fields.prompt: What sound or sound category do you want to try?
fields.helperText: Examples: fan, rain, water, nature, music, broadband sound.

fields.label: Device or source
fields.prompt: Phone speaker, bedside speaker, sound machine, hearing aids, other
fields.helperText: Name the source you can realistically use.

fields.label: Easy time or place
fields.prompt: Where would sound therapy be easiest to use?
fields.helperText: Start where the setup is simple.

fields.label: Difficult time or place
fields.prompt: Where might it be harder to use sound?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Daily plan
fields.prompt: What is your simple plan for trying sound therapy?
fields.helperText: Include when, where, and how you will keep the sound comfortable.

fields.label: Reflection after practice
fields.prompt: What did you notice after trying the plan?
fields.helperText: Optional. You can edit this later.

definitions.title: Tug-of-War Reflection
definitions.purpose: Identify what pulling the rope looks like and what dropping the rope could mean.
definitions.instructions: Acceptance does not mean liking tinnitus or giving up. This reflection looks for a different relationship to the struggle.

fields.label: What I am fighting
fields.prompt: What part of the tinnitus experience are you fighting with?
fields.helperText: Name the struggle in plain words.

fields.label: Pulling the rope looks like
fields.prompt: What do you do when the struggle takes over?
fields.helperText: Examples might include overchecking, arguing with the sound, or avoiding life.

fields.label: Dropping the rope could look like
fields.prompt: What would stepping out of the struggle look like?
fields.helperText: This can be small and imperfect.

fields.label: One useful action
fields.prompt: What is one useful next action?
fields.helperText: Choose something workable today.

definitions.title: Yes AND Builder
definitions.purpose: Hold a real frustration and one useful next action together.
definitions.instructions: Write an honest difficulty, then add one workable action. This is not forced positivity.

fields.label: YES / honest frustration
fields.prompt: Yes, this is hard because...
fields.helperText: Name the difficulty plainly.

fields.label: AND / useful action
fields.prompt: And I can...
fields.helperText: Choose one small next step.

fields.label: Full statement preview
fields.helperText: {yes_statement} AND {and_action}

fields.label: Optional reflection
fields.prompt: What did this help you notice?
fields.helperText: This can stay blank.

definitions.title: Reconnection with What Matters
definitions.purpose: Identify a valued activity affected by tinnitus and one small step toward re-engagement.
definitions.instructions: Look for low-hanging fruit: a step small enough to try without needing the whole problem solved.

fields.label: Valued activity
fields.prompt: What activity or role matters to you?
fields.helperText: Think of something tinnitus has crowded out or complicated.

fields.label: How tinnitus gets in the way
fields.prompt: How does tinnitus interfere?
fields.helperText: Keep the wording factual and kind.

fields.label: Possible steps
fields.prompt: What are a few possible small steps?
fields.helperText: List options without judging them yet.

fields.label: Low-hanging fruit step
fields.prompt: Which step feels easiest to try first?
fields.helperText: Small counts.

fields.label: When I will try it
fields.prompt: When might you try this?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: Deep Breath Check-In Reflection
definitions.purpose: Use one breath as a brief present-moment reset.
definitions.instructions: This is a short check-in, not a test of relaxation or silence. If it increases distress, switch to a grounding or distress-tolerance tool.

fields.label: Situation
fields.prompt: Where were you or what was happening?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: What I noticed before
fields.prompt: What did you notice before the breath?
fields.helperText: Body, mind, sound, or emotion can all count.

fields.label: What I noticed after
fields.prompt: What did you notice after one breath?
fields.helperText: No change is also useful information.

fields.label: Takeaway
fields.prompt: What is one takeaway?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: 3-2-1 Senses
definitions.purpose: Widen attention beyond tinnitus using simple sensory noticing.
definitions.instructions: Notice what is present without trying to force tinnitus away.

fields.label: Three things seen
fields.prompt: Name three things you can see.
fields.helperText: Simple objects are enough.

fields.label: Two things felt or heard
fields.prompt: Name two sensations or sounds.
fields.helperText: Include non-tinnitus sensations or sounds if possible.

fields.label: One sound outside tinnitus
fields.prompt: Name one sound outside tinnitus.
fields.helperText: If the room is quiet, choose a subtle sound or body sensation.

fields.label: What shifted
fields.prompt: What changed in attention, if anything?
fields.helperText: Optional. No shift is acceptable.

definitions.title: Mindful Listening
definitions.purpose: Practice broad listening during an everyday activity.
definitions.instructions: Let tinnitus be one sound among many rather than the only sound that matters.

fields.label: Activity
fields.prompt: What everyday activity did you choose?
fields.helperText: Example: making tea, walking, sitting outside.

fields.label: Environmental sounds
fields.prompt: What sounds did you notice around you?
fields.helperText: List ordinary sounds without ranking them.

fields.label: Body sounds or sensations
fields.prompt: What body sensations or body sounds did you notice?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Tinnitus label
fields.prompt: How could you label tinnitus neutrally?
fields.helperText: Example: “ringing is here.” Optional.

fields.label: Reflection
fields.prompt: What did you notice about broad listening?
fields.helperText: Keep it brief and nonjudgmental.

definitions.title: Sound Shifting
definitions.purpose: Practice moving attention among tinnitus, external sound, body, and the room.
definitions.instructions: This is attention flexibility practice, not exposure therapy and not a requirement to ignore tinnitus.

fields.label: External sound
fields.prompt: What outside sound did you use as an anchor?
fields.helperText: Choose something available and comfortable.

fields.label: Body anchor
fields.prompt: What body sensation did you use, if any?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Tinnitus observation
fields.prompt: What did you notice when attention touched tinnitus?
fields.helperText: Optional. Use neutral wording.

fields.label: What shifted
fields.prompt: What changed as you moved attention?
fields.helperText: No dramatic change is needed.

fields.label: Adjustment needed
fields.prompt: What would make this easier next time?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: STOP
definitions.purpose: Pause before reacting during a tinnitus fluctuation.
definitions.instructions: Distress tolerance tools are for cooling the moment down. They are not crisis care; if you are unsafe, seek immediate help.

fields.label: Safety boundary
fields.helperText: If you may harm yourself or someone else, or you cannot stay safe, use emergency or crisis resources rather than this app.

fields.label: Situation
fields.prompt: What was happening?
fields.helperText: Avoid detailed crisis narratives. A few words are enough.

fields.label: Stop note
fields.prompt: What helped you pause?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Take a breath note
fields.prompt: What did one breath or step back do?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Observe body, thoughts, emotions, urges
fields.prompt: What did you observe?
fields.helperText: Use short labels if that is easier.

fields.label: Proceed mindfully action
fields.prompt: What is one next action that fits the moment?
fields.helperText: Choose something safe and workable.

definitions.title: Temperature/Ice
definitions.purpose: Use temperature as a noticeable sensory reset, not pain.
definitions.instructions: The purpose is noticeable sensory input. Do not cause pain, injury, or unsafe discomfort.

fields.label: Not pain-based
fields.helperText: Use a safe, brief temperature cue. Wrap the ice or choose another cool object if direct ice is too intense. Stop if it hurts.

fields.label: Situation
fields.prompt: What was happening?
fields.helperText: Optional. Keep it brief.

fields.label: What I noticed physically
fields.prompt: What temperature or body sensation did you notice?
fields.helperText: Stay with observable sensations.

fields.label: What changed in attention
fields.prompt: Did attention shift in any way?
fields.helperText: Optional. No shift is okay.

fields.label: Safety or comfort adjustment
fields.prompt: What adjustment would keep this safe or comfortable?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: TIPP
definitions.purpose: Use body-based tools to cool down a high-distress moment.
definitions.instructions: Choose only safe, appropriate options for your body and situation. This is not about pain or unsafe exercise.

fields.label: Choose safely
fields.helperText: Use temperature, movement, breathing, or muscle release only in ways that are medically and physically safe for you. Stop if anything feels unsafe.

fields.label: Situation
fields.prompt: What was happening?
fields.helperText: Keep this brief and non-crisis-focused.

fields.label: Skill used
fields.prompt: Which TIPP option did you use?
fields.helperText: Temperature, movement, paced breathing, muscle release, or another safe body-based option.

fields.label: Before note
fields.prompt: What did you notice before using it?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: After note
fields.prompt: What did you notice after using it?
fields.helperText: A small shift counts.

fields.label: What helped
fields.prompt: What part was most useful?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: The Frozen Orange
definitions.purpose: Use temperature, texture, scent, and changing sensation as grounding.
definitions.instructions: Use a safe sensory object. The point is grounding through noticing, not pain.

fields.label: Situation
fields.prompt: What was happening?
fields.helperText: Optional. Keep it brief.

fields.label: Temperature, texture, scent notes
fields.prompt: What did you notice about temperature, texture, or scent?
fields.helperText: Use simple sensory words.

fields.label: What changed over time
fields.prompt: What changed as the object warmed or your attention shifted?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Attention shift
fields.prompt: What happened to your attention?
fields.helperText: A small or temporary shift counts.

fields.label: Takeaway
fields.prompt: What is one takeaway?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: Distortion Detective
definitions.purpose: Identify a distressing thought and name the closest thinking pattern.
definitions.instructions: Naming a pattern is a way to get perspective. It is not a diagnosis and not a requirement to argue with yourself.

fields.label: Distressing thought
fields.prompt: What thought showed up?
fields.helperText: Use the words your mind used.

fields.label: Closest pattern or custom name
fields.prompt: Which thinking pattern fits best?
fields.helperText: Use a listed pattern or your own plain-language label.

fields.label: Why this pattern fits
fields.prompt: What makes this pattern seem relevant?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: More balanced perspective
fields.prompt: What is a more balanced way to view this?
fields.helperText: Balanced means realistic, not forced-positive.

definitions.title: Evidence For-and-Against
definitions.purpose: Reality-check a distressing tinnitus or sleep-related thought.
definitions.instructions: Write the thought, look at evidence on both sides, then try a balanced statement. This is not forced positivity.

fields.label: Distressing thought
fields.prompt: What thought are you reality-checking?
fields.helperText: Use a tinnitus or sleep-related thought.

fields.label: Evidence for
fields.prompt: What facts seem to support the thought?
fields.helperText: Keep this factual, not a verdict.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.prompt: What facts do not fit the thought?
fields.helperText: Look for missing context, exceptions, or alternative explanations.

fields.label: Balanced statement
fields.prompt: What is a more balanced way to say this?
fields.helperText: Balanced does not mean cheerful. It should be realistic and usable.

fields.label: Optional pattern/distortion label
fields.prompt: Example: all-or-nothing, fortune telling, catastrophizing
fields.helperText: Use this only if it helps.

definitions.title: Re-Scripting a Self-Critical Thought
definitions.purpose: Respond to self-criticism with the same care you might offer someone else.
definitions.instructions: This exercise practices validation and self-compassion without pretending everything is easy.

fields.label: Self-critical thought
fields.prompt: What did the self-critical voice say?
fields.helperText: Write the thought as it showed up.

fields.label: How it affects me
fields.prompt: What happens when this thought runs the show?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: What I would say to someone I care about
fields.prompt: How would you respond to a friend or loved one?
fields.helperText: Use a kind but honest tone.

fields.label: Compassionate rewrite
fields.prompt: How could you say this to yourself with more care?
fields.helperText: This can be realistic and still supportive.

fields.label: Short mantra or reminder
fields.prompt: What short phrase might help later?
fields.helperText: Optional.

definitions.title: DEAR MAN Builder
definitions.purpose: Make a clear request or explain a tinnitus-related need.
definitions.instructions: Build a simple script. The app does not send it anywhere.

fields.label: Describe the situation
fields.prompt: What is the situation?
fields.helperText: Keep this factual.

fields.label: Express how it affects me
fields.prompt: How does it affect you?
fields.helperText: Use clear, non-blaming language.

fields.label: Assert the request
fields.prompt: What are you asking for?
fields.helperText: Make the request specific if possible.

fields.label: Reinforce why it matters
fields.prompt: Why would this help or matter?
fields.helperText: Explain the practical benefit.

fields.label: Mindful, confident, negotiation note
fields.prompt: What do you want to remember while communicating?
fields.helperText: Optional. This can include staying on topic, appearing confident, or being open to negotiation.

definitions.title: Bedtime Sound Plan
definitions.purpose: Plan sound use at night without turning sleep into a test.
definitions.instructions: Use comfortable sound as a settling support. It does not have to force sleep to be useful.

fields.label: Sleep scope
fields.helperText: This is educational sleep support, not a full sleep-treatment program. Keep the plan gentle and adjustable.

fields.label: Sound choice
fields.prompt: What sound might support bedtime?
fields.helperText: Examples: fan, rain, steady sound, soft music, sound machine.

fields.label: Device or source
fields.prompt: What will play the sound?
fields.helperText: Choose something practical and safe for the bedroom.

fields.label: Volume or comfort note
fields.prompt: How will you keep the sound comfortable?
fields.helperText: Avoid turning this into a test of perfect sleep.

fields.label: When I will use it
fields.prompt: When will you start or stop the sound?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: If it is not helping
fields.prompt: What will you do if the sound is not helping?
fields.helperText: Optional. Adjusting or stopping can be part of the plan.

definitions.title: Negative Sleep Thought Reframing
definitions.purpose: Apply cognitive reframing to a sleep-related thought.
definitions.instructions: This is educational support, not a full CBT-I or BBTI program.

fields.label: Sleep scope
fields.helperText: Use this as a reflection tool. If sleep problems are severe, persistent, or medically concerning, consider appropriate sleep or health care.

fields.label: Sleep thought
fields.prompt: What sleep-related thought are you reframing?
fields.helperText: Use the thought as it appeared.

fields.label: Possible thought pattern
fields.prompt: Does a thinking pattern fit?
fields.helperText: Optional.

fields.label: Evidence for
fields.prompt: What facts seem to support the thought?
fields.helperText: Keep this factual.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.prompt: What facts do not fit the thought?
fields.helperText: Include exceptions or missing context.

fields.label: Balanced sleep statement
fields.prompt: What is a more balanced sleep statement?
fields.helperText: Realistic and usable is enough.
